Hi, I'm Nicole Zhan.

I'm a third-year biomedical engineering student. I've spent my co-op terms on materials research at Harvard, quality and regulatory work at a neurotech startup, and hardware compliance at a surgical-safety company. I like working on medical devices from the bench all the way to the paperwork.

About

I'm in the biomedical engineering co-op program at Waterloo. So far my terms have covered a pretty wide range: formulating and characterizing materials in a lab, building the fixtures to test them, and writing the SOPs and risk analyses that keep a device compliant with Health Canada, the FDA, and the TGA.

This past summer I was in the Aizenberg Lab at Harvard SEAS, looking at how surfactants and polymers affect wetting and transport at a biological membrane. Before that I did three terms in Toronto at Omniscient Neurotechnology and Surgical Safety Technologies.

I'm currently looking for co-op roles in medical devices, biomaterials, or R&D.
